messages:
javier: Hi team, onboarding question: I'm on macOS Sonoma (M1) and trying to mirror the infra team's dev setup. I installed asdf and added nodejs/python plugins, but when I launch VS Code the integrated terminal picks up Homebrew node even though `asdf current nodejs` shows 20.7.0. Also my dotfiles set a funky PATH helper that I suspect is the culprit. Any quick debugging tips?
tara: Hey Javier, welcome! First quick checks: `which -a node`, `echo $PATH`, and `asdf which node`. If `which -a` shows /opt/homebrew/bin before ~/.asdf/shims then PATH order is the issue.
javier: `which -a node` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/node then /Users/javier/.asdf/shims/node. `asdf which node` points to the shim at ~/.asdf/shims/node.
phil: Sounds like your shell rc ordering. If you use zsh: ensure asdf init runs after you set PATH helpers. I usually put 

# at end of ~/.zshrc
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"
source "$HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh"

Also run `hash -r` to clear cached command paths.
javier: I have dotfiles that add /opt/homebrew to PATH in a helper function that's sourced late. Could that be overriding?
tara: Yep, if that helper runs after asdf init it can push Homebrew earlier. Move the asdf export to the very top of your interactive rc or source asdf after your helpers to ensure shims are first.
phil: One more wrinkle: VS Code on mac sometimes launches login shells via zprofile. Put the asdf init into both ~/.zprofile and ~/.zshrc (or ~/.zprofile only for login shells). We added that to the onboarding doc.
infra-bot: Note: task OG-221: "Add note: asdf init in zprofile for macOS GUI apps" exists in onboarding backlog.
javier: After moving asdf init to ~/.zprofile and adding shims to PATH top, VS Code terminal now shows the asdf node first. However, npm global installs still go to /usr/local and shadow yarn installed via asdf. How do you recommend handling npm globals?
phil: We recommend avoiding globals, but if you need them set a user prefix: `mkdir -p ~/.npm-global && npm config set prefix '~/.npm-global'` and add `export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"` to your rc. If you want globals to live inside the active asdf node, set prefix to the asdf install path for that node version.
javier: That worked. Last weirdness: I had created a venv and a pnpm store before fixing PATH, and now my IDE uses the wrong interpreter. Should I recreate those?
tara: Yes, delete and recreate venvs and node_modules installed with the wrong interpreter. Doc-wrangler: can we add a short bullet under "mac dev bootstrap" about recreating envs after fixing PATH?
doc-wrangler: Good idea, I'll add a one-liner in the onboarding doc: "If you fix PATH ordering after creating envs, recreate virtualenvs/node_modules so they bind to the correct runtime." Filed DOC-1053.
javier: Thanks all, smooth again :thumbsup:
